coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 7 units (the domain directory itself plus 21.01, 21.02, 21.03, 21.04, 21.05, 21.08), 41 .md files. Matches the expected 7 units / 41 files exactly. 21.06, 21.07 and 21.09 are flat feature files that live in the domain directory and were audited as part of the domain-root unit. Every file was read in full through the 3a implementer-simulation / 3b rubric / 3c devil's-advocate cycle; no sampling. Dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity) scored against the Role Matrix / Role Lens present in each unit; dimensions 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) marked N/A throughout because they are owned by meta/constraints.md, meta/problem-statement.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, none of which is in this domain's scope. Roughly 30 candidate findings were generated in 3a and dropped in 3c: the recurring 'N days' silence threshold in 21.02.02/21.02.03 is explicitly owned and tracked by 21.03.03 ('N is a threshold set at /write-be-spec'); 21.02-cx CX-02's 'applies weakly to 21.02.04' is compatible with 21.02.06's explicit per-channel radio budget; 21.05.03 D-01 ('pay-for-consideration only') vs PAYOLA_CONSIDERATION_HELD is explicitly reconciled by Q-01 and the edge-case table; 21.05-cx CX-01 Q5's 'unresolved' running-campaign question is closed by 21.05.03 Q-02; 21.04.03's late-click behaviour is fixed by 21.04.04 CX-04/Q-02; 21.09 D-04's cross-reference to 21.04.04 D-01/DT-01 resolves correctly; 21.05.02 D-03's 'still up after N days' was dropped because the feature is placed Won't in the MoSCoW ledger.

findings.claim: 21.02.05 states that when two embargoes bind one asset 'the earliest lift governs what is actually public', which cannot be satisfied together with the file's own definition of an embargo as a timestamp before which content must not become public. Under the stated rule the platform releases the asset at the earlier lift time and thereby breaks the second, still-active embargo — the exact outcome the feature exists to prevent. No marker, no tracked question, and no rule anywhere in the tree says which lift time gates the publish path.
findings.evidence: 21.02.05-embargo-premiere-exclusives.md:64 — '| Two embargoes on one asset (print exclusive + radio first-play) | Not merged — separate objects, separate lift times, both binding | Both shown; the earliest lift governs what is actually public |'. Contradicts 21.02.05-embargo-premiere-exclusives.md:26 — 'An embargo is an object: bound content, lift timestamp, bound parties' and :22-23 'An embargo is a timestamp before which specified content must not become public' (as restated in 21.02-pitching-outreach-cx.md:22-23), and :59 '| Artist or Producer posts inside the window via 21.06 | Blocked before publication — this is the feature's primary job |'. 21.02-pitching-outreach-cx.md:36 confirms the multi-embargo model without resolving the gate: 'Two embargoes on one asset (a print exclusive and a radio first-play) must be modelled as separate objects with separate lift times, not merged.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the publish gate for an asset bound by N embargoes releases at min(lift) or max(lift) — i.e. whether a second, later-lifting exclusive is enforced at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An artist gives a print outlet an exclusive lifting 2026-09-04 09:00 and a radio station a first-play lifting 2026-09-06 07:00 on the same track. Implementer A reads line 64 literally and unblocks the smart link, the scheduled beats and the EPK audio at 09:00 on 04 September; the radio first-play is destroyed before it happens and the station's exclusive is worthless. Implementer B reads lines 22-23 and 59 and holds everything until 07:00 on 06 September; the print outlet's piece goes live two days before the platform will serve the link it points at. Both implementations are defensible from the text and they are mutually exclusive.

findings.claim: 21.09 specifies two mutually exclusive behaviours for an EPK whose credits are not yet confirmed in domain 02 — hard block, or include-marked-claimed — joined by a bare 'Or', with no rule for which applies. The States table lists only the blocking branch, and D-03 repeats the same unresolved disjunction. No open question covers it.
findings.evidence: 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:63 — '| Credits not yet confirmed in 02 | The EPK cannot claim credits the credit graph has not confirmed … | Blocked on the unconfirmed credit, with a link to 02. Or included as **claimed**, visibly distinguished. Never silently rendered as verified |'. 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:79 States table carries only '| Blocked | Credits unconfirmed in 02 | Named blocker; the alternative is claiming what we cannot verify |'. 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:116 D-03 — 'Unverified credits are blocked or marked claimed, never rendered as verified'.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an unconfirmed credit blocks EPK assembly/sharing or degrades to a claimed-badge render, and — if both are offered — who chooses.
findings.failure_scenario: An artist assembles a tour EPK the week a session player has not yet confirmed their credit in 02. Implementer A renders the Blocked state and the artist cannot share the EPK with the promoter who asked for it today. Implementer B renders the credit with a 'claimed' badge and the EPK ships. The two products differ in whether the platform can withhold a user's press kit over a third party's inaction — a product decision, not a display choice.

findings.claim: The badge `verified-at-timestamp` is given two incompatible definitions inside the same unit. promotion-marketing-cx.md defines it as an item that was verified and whose link has since changed (i.e. the link-rot case); 21.07, which owns the taxonomy, defines it as a live-but-mutable source (a playlist add) and routes link rot to a separate `Decayed` state. The DQ-20.1 correction notice on CX-05 is explicitly scoped to the pitch-provenance gloss and does not touch this.
findings.evidence: promotion-marketing-cx.md:183-184 — '**verified** (a fixed artefact — an article at a live, retrievable URL — *whether or not a WeJammin pitch produced it*), **verified-at-timestamp** (was verified, link since changed), and **claimed** (typed by the artist, unverifiable)'. 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:90 — '| Verified-at-timestamp | Live but mutable source confirmed (playlist add) | Marked verified as of a date, with the evidence named; weaker than a fixed article, stronger than a typed claim (DT-03) |'; 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:92 — '| Decayed | Source link rotted | Verification lapses; the artist is told before the EPK quietly weakens |'; 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:143 D-05 — 'verified (fixed article), verified-at-timestamp (mutable playlist add), claimed (typed / self-attested)'.
findings.forcedInvention: Which trigger sets `verified-at-timestamp` — artefact mutability at capture, or subsequent link change on a previously-verified item.
findings.failure_scenario: A magazine review verified in March has its URL changed in June. An implementer working from promotion-marketing-cx.md sets the item to `verified-at-timestamp` and the EPK still shows a verification badge; an implementer working from 21.07 sets it to `Decayed`, which is not one of the three renderable strengths. The same coverage item therefore renders as verified-with-a-date on one build and as an undefined/absent badge on the other.

findings.claim: 21.07's `Decayed` state has no defined rendering on the EPK, which is the only surface that renders coverage strength. D-05 fixes exactly three strengths and 21.09 renders 'the strength 21.07 computed'; `Decayed` is a fourth state with no corresponding badge. The playlist-add decay path is specified ('decays toward claimed'); the article link-rot path is not.
findings.evidence: 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:92 — '| Decayed | Source link rotted | Verification lapses; the artist is told before the EPK quietly weakens |' and :72 '| Link rots — the outlet folds, the article vanishes | … | The verification claim decays with the link |', against :81 which does specify the playlist path — 'badge decays toward claimed unless a snapshot was captured'. 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:43-45 — 'The EPK renders the strength 21.07 computed — `verified` / `verified-at-timestamp` / `claimed`'. promotion-marketing-cx.md:187-189 requires the propagation without naming the target — 'Badge decay — a verified link that later rots — must propagate to every EPK that embedded the quote, or the EPK asserts a verification it can no longer stand behind.'
findings.forcedInvention: What badge a decayed article quote renders as on the EPK — `claimed`, `verified-at-timestamp`, a fourth badge, or removal from the kit.
findings.failure_scenario: A 2025 review that fed three sent EPKs 404s in 2026. Implementer A demotes the quote to `claimed` by analogy with the playlist row; Implementer B keeps `verified-at-timestamp` because the item was verified at a date; Implementer C introduces a fourth 'verification lapsed' badge, which is a rendering surface D-07 and 21.09 D-05 explicitly declined to open. All three change what a journalist reads on an EPK already in their inbox.

findings.claim: 21.07 Q-01 is deferred to a stage that has already run and did not answer it. The MoSCoW pass placed 21.07 in the Should band but says nothing about whether automated coverage monitoring is in scope — the question Q-01 actually asks. Every other still-open question in this domain that outlived its target carries an explicit '**Re-targeted**' note; this row does not, so its tracking is malformed rather than merely pending.
findings.evidence: 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:151 — '| Q-01 | Is automated coverage monitoring in scope, or is the log manual-first? Manual is honest and depends on artists doing work they may not do. Monitoring is a real capability with a real cost and a real false-positive problem (DT-02). | User | MoSCoW |'. moscow-ledger.md:463 shows the pass ran and placed the feature without touching monitoring — '| 21.07 | Coverage & Clipping Log | … DT-01 is the domain's single most important finding: verified coverage is a provenance fact structurally identical to a verified credit …'. Contrast the sibling rows that were re-pointed, e.g. 21.06-social-publishing-cross-post.md:109 ('**RESOLVED — built, but at `Could`; not cut.** The MoSCoW pass ratified D-04's honest proposal exactly') and promotion-marketing-index.md:159 Q-09.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the coverage log ships manual-first or with an automated monitoring/suggestion pipeline — a materially different build and cost, currently owned by a discharged stage.
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream stage reads the Deferred-To column, sees 'MoSCoW', checks the ledger, finds the feature placed and the question unaddressed, and has no stage to route it to. The monitoring capability (with its false-positive machinery, D-02's suggestion-with-confirmation flow, and the Detected/Suggested state at 21.07:88) is either built speculatively or silently dropped, and the States table's `Detected` row becomes either dead spec or unbudgeted work.

findings.claim: The domain index's Children table and its accompanying note assert a status for every child that contradicts the children's own headers. The note claims all children are `[SURFACE]` and 'not yet deepened', but five of the six sub-domain indexes are `[BREADTH]`, two of the three flat features are `[PARTIAL]`, and two grandchildren plus the domain CX are `[DEEP]`.
findings.evidence: promotion-marketing-index.md:62-63 — '> 8 children from 12 candidates: 6 sub-domains, 2 features, plus 1 Deep Think addition (21.09). > All `[SURFACE]` — classified and outlined, not yet deepened.' and the Children table rows :67-75, every one of which reads '`[SURFACE]`'. Actual headers on disk: 21.01-release-campaign-planner-index.md:5 '**Status**: [BREADTH]'; 21.02-pitching-outreach-index.md:5 '[BREADTH]'; 21.03-pitch-targets-crm-index.md:5 '[BREADTH]'; 21.04-smart-links-presave-attribution-index.md:5 '[BREADTH]'; 21.05-paid-promotion-index.md:5 '[BREADTH]'; 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:5 '[PARTIAL]'; 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:5 '[PARTIAL]'; and 21.02.06 / 21.05.03 / promotion-marketing-cx.md all carry '[DEEP]'.
findings.forcedInvention: Which status record is authoritative for pipeline gating — the parent's table or each child's own header.
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream workflow that gates on ideation depth (deep-dive completeness, or the audit-scope enumeration itself) reads the domain index, concludes nothing under 21 has been deepened, and either re-runs deepening over 41 already-deepened files or skips 21.07/21.09/21.02.06/21.05.03 as not-yet-ready when they are the most developed files in the domain.

findings.claim: The domain Role Matrix gives the Producer read-only access across 21.01, but 21.01's own Role Matrix and 21.01.02's Role Lens give the Producer ⚙️ Config — a write capability (marking their own asset rows final, and flagging a recall). The domain-level rollup understates the access rather than summarising it, and the accompanying reading note reinforces the wrong version by characterising every Producer row as a view.
findings.evidence: promotion-marketing-index.md:101 — '| 21.01 Release Campaign Planner | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only | ❌ None | ❌ None |' with the note at :118-122 — 'Producer''s `👁️` rows are narrow and real … They see the deadline that binds them (21.01) … Every one is a constraint or a reputational fact, never a marketing view'. Against 21.01-release-campaign-planner-index.md:37 — '| 21.01.02 Asset Readiness Gate | ✅ Full | ⚙️ Config | ❌ None | ❌ None |' and 21.01.02-asset-readiness-gate.md:20 — 'Producer | Config | Owns and marks state on **their** rows only — master final, stems delivered, alternate/instrumental mixes, ISRC-ready file spec. Can flag a recall on an asset they previously marked final.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the Producer holds any write capability inside 21.01 at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A spec writer working from the domain Role Matrix (the file the pipeline reads first) provisions the Producer read-only across the release campaign planner. The Producer's mark-final action never gets built, and with it the event that 21.01.02's happy path step 5 hangs on — 'Gate flips the row green; the dependent grid row clears its blocker; distributor delivery in domain 12 is now unblocked' — leaving the readiness gate with no writer for the rows only the Producer owns.

findings.claim: The asset gate's `At risk` state is triggered by an unbound literal placeholder ('within N days') and by a colour term ('Red') that is not one of the states the same table defines. The at-risk window drives escalation to the Musician and the campaign risk roll-up, and no open question in this unit or its parent binds either term.
findings.evidence: 21.01.02-asset-readiness-gate.md:69 — '| At risk | Red or not-started within N days of a hard deadline | Escalated in the roll-up and to the Musician |'. The same States table (:63-70) enumerates Loading, Empty, Not started, In progress, Ready, Was-final, At risk, Blocked — there is no Red state. 'Red' is used normatively elsewhere without definition: 21.01.02-asset-readiness-gate.md:19 'Chases the ones that are red. … 2 assets red, 1 blocking a hard deadline in 6 days'; 21.01.01-backward-planned-campaign-grid.md:73 '| At-risk | A hard row''s dependent asset is red near its deadline |'; 21.01-release-campaign-planner-cx.md:33 'a red asset flags the dependent deadline at risk' and :35 'An asset going red near its deadline must notify the Musician'. Open Questions in 21.01.02 (:98-99) cover clearance and machine-checkable specs only; 21.01.01 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover DSP mechanics, rule maintenance and campaign cardinality.
findings.forcedInvention: The numeric at-risk window (N), and which of the defined gate states 'red' denotes.
findings.failure_scenario: Implementer A sets N = 3 and maps 'red' to Not started only; Implementer B sets N = 14 and maps 'red' to Not started plus In progress plus Was-final. On the same campaign, A's roll-up shows zero at-risk assets ten days before the master deadline while B's escalates four — and the escalation ladder on hard rows, which the domain exists to make unmissable, fires on entirely different days.

findings.claim: 21.03.01 states the per-sender pitch budget as a specific number and attributes it to 21.02.06, but 21.02.06 — which owns the caps — sets a different number on a different window. Neither statement is marked, and the two files disagree by 20% on the value the directory's own core argument (the cost of a stale contact) is built on.
findings.evidence: 21.03.01-media-target-directory.md:80 DT-01 — 'a *stale* contact costs a pitch from a budget of 8 per week (21.02.06), plus the false belief that they were rejected when in fact nobody read it'. Against 21.02.06-pitch-rate-limits-curator-protection.md:33-36 — '**Per-sender caps** … Default: **10 pitches per channel per rolling 7 days**, where a consumed pitch returns to the budget 7 days after it was sent — not a fixed weekly calendar reset', restated at :107 '| Empty | New sender, no pitches sent on this channel yet | Full budget shown ("10 of 10 pitches this week")'.
findings.forcedInvention: The per-sender cap value and its window semantics when reading 21.03.01 as a source.
findings.failure_scenario: A spec writer sizing the directory's freshness UI (how loudly staleness must be surfaced given how scarce a pitch is) or a downstream copy string works from 21.03.01's '8 per week' and produces budget affordances inconsistent with the 10-per-channel rolling-7-day model 21.02.06 actually enforces; the composer shows one remaining-budget figure and the directory implies another.

findings.claim: Two open questions in this unit are deferred to MoSCoW, a stage that has already run and that answered the question by implication without either row being updated. Unlike every other outlived row in this domain, neither carries a '**Re-targeted**' or 'RESOLVED' note, so the beachhead question is left pointing at a discharged stage.
findings.evidence: 21.04-smart-links-presave-attribution-index.md:70 — '| Q-02 | Is this sub-domain the **beachhead**? `meta/problem-statement.md` Q-03 asks which consolidation surface wins users first. … It is a plausible wedge and a plausible waste. | User | MoSCoW |'. 21.04.01-smart-link-builder.md:128 — '| Q-02 | Is this the beachhead? See Q-02 on the sub-domain index. | User | MoSCoW |'. The pass ran and settled it against this sub-domain — promotion-marketing-index.md:159 records 'RESOLVED — the MoSCoW pass ran … **D-31**''s release split puts 21 outside both windows — "**v1 — session spine** (01, 02, 05, 07, **09-capture**)" and "**v1.5 — marketplaces** (13, 14, 15)" — so it is phase-2+, and the beachhead is decided and is not this domain.'
findings.forcedInvention: Nothing product-shaped; the defect is that a settled decision remains recorded as open against a stage that cannot take it again, so a downstream reader must decide whether the beachhead question is live.
findings.failure_scenario: A /create-prd session collecting owner decisions reads 21.04's two open rows, finds a beachhead question apparently still awaiting a MoSCoW pass, and either re-opens sequencing that D-31 already locked or spends owner time on a question the ledger answered — the same failure the parent's Q-09 was updated to prevent.

findings.claim: 21.04.02 D-03 makes grant expiry a values-grade rule ('grants expire; they are not held indefinitely') and the Void state is triggered by a grant that has 'aged out', but no horizon is given for either the cancelled-release case or the aged-out case. Q-02 tracks per-DSP OAuth token lifetimes — a provider fact — not the platform's own retention rule for a held library-write authorisation.
findings.evidence: 21.04.02-presave-preadd-authorization.md:114 D-03 — 'Grants expire; they are not held indefinitely against a cancelled release | Perpetual library-write authorisation for a record that will never exist is indefensible.'; :90 '| Void | Release cancelled / grant aged out | Expired rather than held forever |'; :59 '| Release is cancelled | Grants never fire and are held indefinitely against nothing | Grants must expire. Holding library-write authorisation forever for a record that will never exist is not defensible |'. Q-02 at :122 scopes only the provider side — 'Exact OAuth scopes available and required per DSP for a library write, and their token lifetimes.'
findings.forcedInvention: The grant-expiry horizon (immediate on cancellation vs a fixed age-out period), and whether an indefinitely-delayed release ages its grants out at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An artist cancels a release six weeks after enabling pre-save. Implementer A voids every outstanding grant at the moment of cancellation; Implementer B ages grants out 180 days after authorisation regardless of release state, so the platform holds live library-write authorisations for a record that will never exist for a further four months — precisely the state D-03 calls indefensible. A third case, a release delayed a year, is not covered by either reading.
